Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "MinebeaMitsumi Inc."
- Document: "MINEBEA CO., LTD."

Minebea Co., Ltd. and MinebeaMitsumi Inc. are actually different legal entities. MinebeaMitsumi Inc. was formed in 2017 when Minebea Co., Ltd. merged/acquired Mitsumi Electric and renamed itself. So in 2011 (the issuing year of the certificate), the applicant was Minebea Co., Ltd. The register saying "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." appears to be an updated/anachronistic company name — the company renamed itself later. But strictly per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." vs "MINEBEA CO., LTD." spelling drift or legal-suffix drift? No — these are genuinely different legal names, historically distinct (Minebea Co., Ltd. renamed to MinebeaMitsumi Inc. in 2017). The certificate, issued in 2011, correctly names Minebea Co., Ltd. as applicant. So the verdict is different-entity, best_value = "MINEBEA CO., LTD." (document's value).

Even though they're the same corporate family (successor entity), the rules say genuinely different company names = different-entity. The document is the legal instrument, and at the time of issuance the applicant was Minebea Co., Ltd.

So:
